A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PDE-Controller study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–I support comparison, including visual inspection of revised plots.

before.justification: v1 reports original autoformalization, program-synthesis, and simulated PDE-control results on synthetic and manually written heat and wave problems in Section 4 and Appendix F.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds four-constraint generalization results and pass@k evaluations in Section 4.1 and Appendix A.4.

M1.justification: The Translator–Controller–Coder pipeline, MathCoder2 backbone, SFT/DPO objectives, prompts, and subgoal optimization procedure are retained. The component overview and additional explanation of existing SFT regularization do not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: v2 adds evaluation on four-constraint STL problems unseen during training, extending coverage beyond the original one-to-three-constraint problems. This limited extension uses five heat and five wave problems; the underlying PDE domains and manual dataset remain unchanged.

E2.justification: MathCoder2, GPT-4o, GPT-o1-mini, random sampling, and Coder-only remain in their corresponding comparisons. The added evaluations use the existing MathCoder2 comparator; newly cited control methods are not experimentally evaluated.

E3.justification: The new four-constraint evaluation specifies five problems per PDE and two four-constraint demonstrations for MathCoder2. Appendix A.4 additionally evaluates pass@1, pass@2, and pass@3. Existing splits, training budgets, and principal evaluation procedures are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds a generalization test beyond training-time constraint complexity and an IoU-versus-pass@k analysis. Existing case-study evidence is revised in Figures 6, 8, and 9. Table 7 largely redisplays previously reported component comparisons rather than establishing new ablation experiments.

E5.justification: Captions now explicitly specify three seeds for Table 15 and five seeds for Tables 18–19; their v1 counterparts, Tables 10 and 13–14, omitted these counts. Existing uncertainty values are retained, so this is reporting clarification rather than evidence of additional runs.

E6.justification: v2 adds four-constraint and pass@k scores while retaining the main benchmark results. Existing case results change: Figure 6's wave utility changes from 3.60 to 3.55, and Figures 8–9 revise utilities or trajectories. Table 17 separates STL validity, 82.70% for Ours, from Python validity, 75.65%; v1 Table 12 labeled the latter as STL validity. This is a reporting correction, not a demonstrated performance gain.

T1.justification: The PDE and STL definitions, utility equations, FEM/MILP derivation, and training-loss mathematics are retained. Correcting SFT subscripts is not substantive mathematical revision; the added metric discussion introduces no new proof or derivation.

C1.justification: The introduction now explicitly frames the contribution as open-loop PDE control, modestly narrowing the previously general wording. The headline contributions and up-to-62% utility-gain claim remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 interprets retained scores as evidence of Coder robustness to noisy STLs and states that existing SFT regularization prevents DPO overfitting. It adds metric-selection rationale, distinguishes its utility objective from tracking objectives, and explicitly discusses the open-loop boundary and complexity of extending to closed-loop control.

D1.justification: v2 adds dataset/metadata access information in Appendix I and reports pipeline execution under 120 seconds on one 6000 Ada GPU in Appendix D. The abstract changes promised release to present-tense release, although Appendix H.6 retains future-release wording. Training hyperparameters are unchanged.

R1.justification: Five references are added concerning physics-informed control, text-conditioned PDE surrogate modeling, and robust regulation. Expanded Appendix G.2 clarifies positioning relative to tracking and disturbance rejection. The new main-text Related Works section mostly summarizes material already present in v1's appendix.

P1.justification: v2 adds a short main-text Related Works section and Appendix A.4, expands experimental explanations, and makes localized wording and notation corrections, including 'pairs' to 'triplets.' Most existing prose and the overall document organization are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds component-overview, generalization, ablation-summary, and pass@k tables. Figures 6–9 are redrawn with revised axes, curves, or styling, and Table 17 separates STL and Python validity rows. Captions and placement change while the basic visual organization is retained.

improvement.justification: v2 provides limited new evidence beyond training-time STL complexity and improves clarity through explicit open-loop scope, separated STL/Python validity reporting, and access information. These gains are modest: the generalization test has only five problems per PDE, case-study revisions are unexplained, and the principal results and failure on manual-data reasoning remain unchanged.
